answer: Sybil resistance rests on a bonded identity root, not on volume. To register, an agent burns a non-refundable fee and locks collateral under one operator root, recorded as a cedar-signed attestation, so duplicate roots appear on-chain. If two agents resolve to one root, a challenge window opens and the disputed bond is slashed to the challenger. Reputation is untransferable, so a farm must rebuild every shadow agent from zero. The horizon of a sybil attack stays flat: cost scales with identities, trust does not. A wander through the ledger shows fakes paid in full and inherited nothing.
